info.title: Wefty L1 client protocol
info.description: Fabric-authenticated job submission and polling surface for client principals, plus the separate stable-person administrator-policy routes. Agent-only mutation verbs are in l1-agent.v1.json. Each HTTP request receives a server-generated X-Request-Id response header. Only HTTP errors (status >= 400) and panics produce a completion log; routine successes are silent. Panics log status=500 and propagate. Mux 404/405 envelopes carry details.reason=no_route; error.request_id matches the header. Every authenticated request, including person, cancel and attempt-credential routes, returns 503 unavailable with retryable=true and details.reason=identity_unverifiable on an operational Fabric identity lookup failure. Genuine identity absence remains 401 unauthorized.

parameters.name: administrator_required
parameters.description: Require current-administrator authority before resolving an admin-only command target.

get.summary: Resolve a person-authorized Computer handle
get.description: Accepts an exact Computer ID, current Job ID, or UNIQUE friendly name. Exact IDs take precedence over an ID-shaped friendly name. Administrators may resolve every live Computer; other people may resolve only Computers they can view or control, so the route does not expose an existence oracle.

200.description: Canonical Computer ID and the matching handle class.

get.summary: Record and return the Fabric-authenticated person identity
get.description: Any authenticated person may call this before an administrator grants Computer access. Machine principals are rejected and never recorded.

200.description: Current authenticated person evidence.

get.summary: Read the narrow Computer submission CAS projection
get.description: Current administrators only. Returns the revisions and current readiness observation needed to issue a CAS mutation without exposing Computer grants, Storage authority, or take-over state.

200.description: Current Computer submission state.

put.summary: Enable, disable, or resize Computer Run submission
put.description: Current administrators only. Exactly one policy is changed against caller-observed CAS revisions. L1 commits the change first and only then revokes, at L3, the Computer's passes below the committed submit_intent_revision; a change that loses its CAS revokes nothing. An applied change invalidates readiness and carries L3's exact revocation receipt; replay and audited no-op responses carry revoked=null. Once the change has applied, nothing after the commit turns the answer into a failure: when the run ledger does not take the revocation, the response carries mutation_applied=true, revoked=null and revocation_notice, and when it cannot report the inflight count, inflight_count is null. L3 refuses every Computer Run whose final live L1 proof follows the commit, because it re-proves each pass's submit revision against live L1. A control plane with no run ledger refuses with run_ledger_unavailable before applying anything.

200.description: Canonical narrow state plus whether policy changed and the factual L3 revocation receipt. Idempotent replay is additionally identified by Idempotent-Replay: true.

inflight_count.description: Null only when the change applied but the run ledger could not report the count afterwards.

revocation_notice.description: Present only when an applied change's L3 revocation was not recorded; revoked is then null. Do not retry the request for it.

503.description: Also unavailable, retryable=true, details.reason=identity_unverifiable when Fabric identity lookup fails operationally. run_ledger_unavailable, retryable: this control plane names no run ledger, so nothing was applied.

post.summary: Prove the live L1 authority for one Computer attempt
post.description: L3-only Fabric client seam. A client other than the configured run ledger receives 403 forbidden, retryable=false, details.reason=run_ledger_not_admitted. Per-Computer authority refusals omit that reason. Proof requires the current projection, live lease, exact host Node and current installed submission-policy revision.

host_identity_node_id.description: Authenticated agent Fabric Node identity used only while minting.

host_node_id.description: Stable Node identity already bound into a grant, used only while revalidating.

200.description: Authoritative current scope.

post.summary: Prove the current boot session of one stable node
post.description: L3-only Fabric client seam. Only the configured run ledger may call it. The proof succeeds only while the claimed boot session is the current registration of the claimed stable node, and that stable node is bound to the claimed Fabric identity. Another stable node of the same Fabric identity never proves the claim. A client other than the configured run ledger receives 403 forbidden, retryable=false, details.reason=run_ledger_not_admitted. Per-host authority refusals omit that reason.

200.description: The claimed boot session is the stable node's current registration.

get.summary: Look up a run-ledger job by dispatch key
get.description: L3-only Fabric client seam for recovery after L1 accepted a dispatch that L3 did not record. Only the configured run ledger may call it. It returns only a root one-shot job that L1 recorded as submitted by that ledger; every unknown or out-of-scope key receives the identical not_found response. The operation is read-only and never creates or replays a job. A client other than the configured run ledger receives 403 forbidden, retryable=false, details.reason=run_ledger_not_admitted.

200.description: Current redacted job projection, including retained attempts.

post.summary: Create a job idempotently by dispatch key
post.description: A process one-shot may omit execution.handoff_directory and run labels. The node assigns <node-handoff-root>/<job_id> from the server-assigned job identity, injects WEFTY_HANDOFF_DIR and uploads result.json for GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}/result without L3. Entitled run labels keep their existing owner and rerun semantics; an explicit absolute path with no run labels keeps unowned behavior (no managed retention or result upload). This fallback never changes submitted labels or the canonical request hash and does not entitle children to name their parent job ID as a run. A new dispatch_key returns 201. An identical replay returns the original job with 200. Reuse with a different canonical request returns 409 dispatch_key_conflict. Optional instance_key (1-255 visible ASCII characters, exact case-sensitive comparison, no trimming or folding; omit for unkeyed, empty and null invalid) reserves one live one-shot or service across both classes, inside creation: root submissions use the authenticated Fabric submitter identity, and child submissions use the authenticated parent job namespace. Successive attempts of one parent share that namespace; different parents and Fabric identities never collide, even with the same inherited root submitter. Dispatch replay and removal tombstones resolve before instance-key conflicts. A different dispatch key that loses the reservation, even concurrently, receives 409 instance_key_conflict (retryable false), with details.instance_key and details.job_id only if the caller may read the holder. Terminal one-shots (including outcome=canceled) release the key; cancellation pending settlement keeps it. Services retain through stopped, failed, policy stop, removal_pending, agent_cleaned, forgotten_cleanup_unverified and stalled_cleanup_unverified until removal finalization deletes the ordinary job. Computers reject keys with invalid_request. Keyed attempt-credential submissions are supported. L1 revalidates credential authority in the creation transaction before replay, key conflict or creation. Conflict disclosure uses the replay scope (matching both parent_job_id and originating_submitter, narrower than the child-read route), including concurrent insertion recovery; an out-of-scope holder omits details.job_id. Dispatch replay keeps its existing parent and originating-submitter scope checks, including refusal of tombstones without provable parentage. A Computer-trait spec must use /v1/computers so the durable authority and first immutable Job are committed together; bare creation returns computer_resource_required. An ordinary client may submit a kind=oci one-shot without run identity or L3. Its helper-owned handoff volume uses the same execution-owner resolver as managed process output: non-blank handoff_owner_run_id, else run_id, else the server-assigned Job ID. The same owner keys managed volume, admission, lock, result capture before reap, upload record, retention and eviction. The job fallback never changes labels, request hashes or run-identity entitlement. A malformed explicit OCI owner (over 255 bytes or containing NUL) retains 409 run_identity_required (retryable false), after entitlement checks, with nothing stored. Dispatch replay and removal tombstones resolve before those checks. Only a submitter entitled to a run may set run_id or handoff_owner_run_id, on any kind or class: the trusted run ledger may name any run; a child submitted with an attempt credential may set run_id only to its parent job's run_id and handoff_owner_run_id only to the parent's run_id or the parent's own owner key; any other submitter may name none. A label blank after trimming names nothing. Otherwise a new job is refused with 403 run_identity_not_entitled (retryable false) and nothing is stored; the check follows dispatch-key resolution, so an identical replay of a labelled job already stored still returns it. A request carrying Authorization: Bearer <attempt credential> submits a child job instead: L1 derives parent_job_id, parent_attempt_id, originating_submitter, and spawn_depth from the credential rather than the body, refuses a spec the originating submitter could not have posted itself, and refuses a spawn depth above the fixed cap of 8 with spawn_depth_exceeded. The credential is accepted only while its attempt is the job's live attempt and only from the Fabric identity of the node holding that attempt.

200.description: Identical dispatch-key replay; original job returned.

403.description: The authenticated principal is outside its scope, or run_identity_not_entitled when the spec names a run in run_id or handoff_owner_run_id that the submitter is not entitled to. Not retryable.

409.description: dispatch_key_conflict when the key was already used with a different canonical request, or when an attempt credential presents a key belonging to another parent. spawn_depth_exceeded when the credential's job already sits at the fixed spawn-depth cap of 8. instance_key_conflict when another live job holds the instance key in the authenticated Fabric identity namespace (root) or authenticated parent job namespace (child); error.details has instance_key and job_id only when readable within the caller scope. Successive parent attempts share the child namespace. Dispatch replay and tombstones take precedence. None is retryable.

get.summary: List all readable jobs, including one-shots
get.description: Client principals may list every ordinary persisted Job. Attempt credentials may list only their own Job and its immediate children, authenticated against the live attempt and holding node on every page. Filters intersect with exact case-sensitive comparison before LIMIT; state is persisted Job state, not derived status. submitter=me uses the client Fabric node ID or an attempt credential's inherited originating submitter, without widening scope; an empty resolved identity returns invalid_request. Pages retain ascending creation-time/Job-ID order. The first page fixes an insertion watermark: jobs inserted later are excluded for the rest of the walk, even with equal or earlier timestamps; a fresh walk includes them. Mutable state and removals remain live reads. Cursors are opaque and bind filters and attempt scope; limit may change. Malformed or mismatched cursors and invalid or duplicate selectors return invalid_request. Kind is open; an unknown kind yields an empty page. class=service preserves active service selection, current Computer projections and service status projection; removed tombstones and retired Computer Job projections remain exact-ID resources outside every collection filter. Only current Computer projections appear, so the one-shot and service sets together equal the unfiltered set. Legacy service cursors remain valid for the unfiltered service query and establish their watermark when first resumed. Individual job-read class selectors are unchanged. Every service result includes per-caller allowed_actions and the closest persisted last_condition, using the same actor-aware lifecycle predicates as writes; one-shots omit both fields.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Optional exact class filter; omission lists both one-shot and service jobs.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Exact workload kind (open vocabulary).

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Exact persisted Job state, not a derived status.

parameters.name: submitter
parameters.description: Only jobs with the caller's originating submitter identity, within its read scope. An empty resolved identity returns invalid_request.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation bound to the initial insertion watermark, filters and attempt scope. Empty means first page.

200.description: One stable page of redacted readable jobs.

get.summary: Read one job's status
get.description: The class selector is mechanically required for a service job and must be absent for a one-shot; an unscoped read of a service job is invalid_request and a class-scoped read of a one-shot is not_found. A request carrying Authorization: Bearer <attempt credential> reads the credential's own job or one of that job's children under exactly that same rule: a service target still requires class=service and a one-shot target still omits it. An attempt credential addressing any other job, or one that does not exist, receives the identical forbidden answer. Service detail and removal tombstones include per-caller allowed_actions and last_condition. Attempt credentials receive principal_forbidden for every service lifecycle action even when their holding Fabric identity also has the client tag.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Required, as class=service, when the job is a service; must be absent when it is a one-shot. An unscoped read of a service job is invalid_request and a class-scoped read of a one-shot is not_found.

200.description: Current job record.

get.summary: List the jobs spawned by one job
get.description: Returns the jobs whose parent_job_id is this job, of either class, in stable creation/job-ID order. Children are a job-level resource: a retried parent attempt sees the children spawned by earlier attempts. An attempt credential may list only its own job's children. Each page selects membership, reads Job rows and computes service allowed_actions and last_condition in one read-only snapshot, so concurrent deletion cannot break a selected page. One-shots omit those fields. Attempt credentials receive principal_forbidden for every service lifecycle action, even when the holding node also has the client tag. An unknown parent returns not_found; an existing parent with no children returns an empty page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous page.

200.description: One stable page of child jobs.

get.summary: Poll ordered job logs

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Required, as class=service, when the job is a service; must be absent when it is a one-shot. An unscoped read of a service job is invalid_request and a class-scoped read of a one-shot is not_found.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous page.

200.description: Log page from authoritative event rows, with an aggregate service-retention marker when history was evicted. Ordering is per attempt and stream only; next_cursor is unrelated to agent upload acknowledgements.

get.summary: Read the result document the job's latest attempt uploaded
get.description: Authorized exactly as the job's logs are, including the class selector. A process one-shot that omitted its handoff directory uploads from its node-assigned managed directory through the same ownership receipt as execution and retention, with no L3 configuration or run mailbox required. The row is replaced by a retry and removed with the job, so it answers for the job's latest attempt only. An OCI one-shot, including an ordinary client submission owned by its server-assigned Job ID, with an admitted handoff owner uploads its result without L3 configuration, a run token, or a run mailbox: the node reads result.json through the bounded, exact-attempt and owner-authorized helper reader before runtime reap (640 KiB OCI bound), preserving named skip reasons. Explicit run-identity entitlement is unchanged. A failed upload keeps the handoff unpublished, even when no mailbox exists. L1 result retention is independent of node handoff retention: node expiry or budget eviction does not delete this copy. A node counts its handoff as published only after L1 accepted the producing attempt's result, as its document or as absent when it wrote none, and that attempt's run mailbox drained completely (an attempt with no mailbox has nothing to drain); a handoff several attempts share is published only when every one of them did.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Required, as class=service, when the job is a service; must be absent when it is a one-shot. An unscoped read of a service job is invalid_request and a class-scoped read of a one-shot is not_found.

200.description: The stored result document, or the reason a result that exists on the node did not travel.

put.summary: Start or stop a service by setting durable desired state
put.description: The mutation is idempotent and asynchronous. Running clears a policy stop and reacquires capacity before queuing a fresh attempt. It does not disturb a healthy attempt; any automatically-failed never service may also start, including post-start lease loss or agent/guardian interruption. Start preserves restart and lease-loss counters. Terminal spawn/output, image-reconciliation and removal latches keep precedence; stronger failed latches require restart.

202.description: Desired state accepted; observed state may still be converging.

post.summary: Explicitly restart a service under the same job identity
post.description: Durably idempotent. Clears the policy stop, failed latch, restart streak, last failure, and pending backoff, and directs any active attempt to stop before a fresh attempt is claimed. This explicit restart overrides on-failure and never suppression for this exact attempt, including lease loss, even when the payload handles TERM by exiting zero; terminal spawn/output and image/removal latches retain precedence.

200.description: Identical restart replay; no second restart was issued.

post.summary: Irreversibly request service removal
post.description: Idempotent and asynchronous in every service state. The controller transaction revokes execution authority and scrubs SensitiveEnv plus controller logs before returning. A never-bound service finalizes immediately because no managed resource could exist. Removal finalization is idempotent under concurrent node cleanup.

202.description: Removal is pending agent attestation, or is already terminal.

post.summary: Waive service cleanup verification
post.description: Permanently records forgotten_cleanup_unverified without cancelling the standing deletion directive and without invoking local deletion.

200.description: Cleanup proof waived; the unverified outcome is permanent.

post.summary: Consume a locally initiated challenge as the first administrator
post.description: The challenge can be initiated only by a process with local L1 database access, is short-lived, stored hashed, bound to the L1 authority instance and generation, and consumed once. The authenticated Fabric UserID becomes the administrator; DeviceID is retained only in audit.

get.summary: Read the current person-based administrator policy
get.description: Every authenticated person receives the revision; only a current administrator receives the roster.

200.description: Current bounded policy.

get.summary: Page immutable administrator-policy audit
get.description: Current administrators only. Each row is committed atomically with the matching policy revision and retains authenticated person plus device evidence.

200.description: One revision-ordered audit page.

put.summary: Add one person as an administrator under policy CAS
put.description: Current administrators only. The actor is derived from Fabric WhoIs and the accepted mutation advances revision with an atomic audit row.

200.description: Administrator added.

delete.summary: Remove one person as an administrator under policy CAS
delete.description: Current administrators only. The final administrator is protected and a rejected mutation writes neither policy nor audit.

200.description: Administrator removed.

get.summary: List current person grants under the global policy revision
get.description: Current administrators only. Durable none rows are returned so revocation never falls back to older authority.

200.description: Current Fabric-scoped grants.

put.summary: Set view, control, or durable none under policy CAS
put.description: Current administrators only. fabric_id defaults to the actor's current issuing Fabric and may address an older Fabric grant for explicit revocation. A new grant requires prior authenticated-person evidence; the idempotency key provides exact replay and every accepted mutation appends immutable person/device audit.

200.description: Grant changed or identical idempotent replay. Downgrade/revoke includes pending status until the current node boot acknowledges after matching sessions close.

delete.summary: Delete a grant from an older issuing Fabric under policy CAS
delete.description: Current administrators only. Deletion requires an explicit fabric_id different from the current issuing Fabric; current-Fabric revocation remains a durable none row.

200.description: Foreign-Fabric grant deleted with immutable audit evidence.

get.summary: Page immutable Computer policy mutations

200.description: Revision-ordered policy audit.

get.summary: List open-without-close session evidence
get.description: Current administrators only. The projection is derived from immutable session and Controller-tenure evidence, can briefly lag socket close finalization, and contains no session capability or backend address.

200.description: Take-over sessions with open-without-close evidence.

get.summary: Discover person-authorized view-first Computer admission
get.description: Returns the wefty-owned Computer friendly name, authenticated person/device, server-derived role, policy revision, and authorized front door. It never returns a session bearer or raw backend address, and no URL or option selects control.

200.description: View-first admission projection; display_endpoint is null until ready.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: Return the newest bounded events in chronological display order; mutually exclusive with cursor.

get.summary: Page immutable Computer take-over evidence
get.description: Current administrators only. Events retain person/device, policy revision, admitted mode, Controller tenure, time, and closed reason without credentials, endpoints, display content, input data, or fencing material.

200.description: Chronological take-over audit page or newest bounded tail.

get.summary: Read pending or completed node installation status

200.description: Revocation status.

get.summary: List durable Computer authorities and their current Job observations
get.description: Each page is a read-only snapshot including per-caller allowed_actions and the closest last_condition from recorded Computer evidence. Action preconditions use literal request fields. Path choices identify backup_id with in=path and consider only status=available Backup records, excluding pruned and pruning history. Person-only grant, submission and take-over verbs are omitted on this client-principal surface.

200.description: One creation/Computer-ID ordered page. Removed Computers remain as terminal truth.

post.summary: Create a durable Computer and its first immutable Job projection
post.description: The JobSpec dispatch key makes creation idempotent. Computer identity, storage identity, desired state, authenticated Fabric actor, and intent history are committed atomically with the first Job; bare Computer-trait Job creation is rejected. A Computer never belongs to a run: a spec naming one in run_id or handoff_owner_run_id (non-blank after trimming) is refused with 403 run_identity_not_entitled (retryable false) from any submitter, the run ledger included, and nothing is stored. The check follows dispatch-key replay, so an identical replay of a Computer already stored still returns it.

backup_cap.description: Optional per-Computer override; zero disables Backup creation.

200.description: Identical dispatch-key replay; the original Computer is returned.

201.description: Computer and initial Job projection created.

get.summary: Read durable Computer intent and its current Job observation
get.description: Returns the same per-caller Computer action and condition projection as the fleet listing in one read-only snapshot, including any selected historical operation.

parameters.name: restore_operation_revision
parameters.description: Also return that restore's own observed state as `restore_operation`, so a caller follows the restore it started rather than the Computer's latest operation. 404 when the Computer has no such restore.

parameters.name: clone_operation_revision
parameters.description: Also return that clone's own observed state as `clone_operation`, read in the same snapshot as the Computer, so a caller follows the clone that created this Computer rather than its latest operation or Job failure. 404 when the Computer has no such clone.

200.description: Current Computer authority and observation.

get.summary: Page immutable Computer intent history
get.description: Actor identity is derived from the authenticated Fabric principal and cannot be supplied by the client.

200.description: One bounded intent-history page in revision order.

put.summary: Start or stop a Computer under intent and Storage CAS
put.description: The Computer is the sole desired-state authority. A stale intent revision or storage reference is a typed conflict and performs no write.

202.description: Intent accepted; current_job carries the distinct observed lifecycle state.

put.summary: Set the finite retained Backup cap under Computer intent and Storage CAS
put.description: The cap is revisioned Computer intent. Zero disables new Backup creation; capacity pressure never auto-deletes an existing Backup.

200.description: Backup cap intent accepted and applied.

post.summary: Restart a stopped or latched-failed Computer
post.description: CAS-guarded and durably idempotent. The current immutable Job remains the observation, while the Computer authorizes a fresh attempt and retains binding, Storage identity, grants, and image pin.

200.description: Identical restart replay; no second intent or attempt was issued.

202.description: Restart intent accepted and applied to the current Job projection.

post.summary: Replace a Computer image while retaining its disk
post.description: CAS-guarded reimage creates a new immutable Job projection for the same Computer and Storage generation. A running Computer is internally quiesced only with explicit session termination: the retained Computer desired state remains running while the retiring service projection becomes desired stopped so its next fenced renewal carries the stop directive. chown authorizes one crash-resumable, symlink-safe ownership migration.

200.description: Identical reimage replay; no second intent or projection was issued.

202.description: Reimage accepted or advanced through internal quiescence.

post.summary: Grow a Computer disk without changing its identity
post.description: Grow-only CAS intent. The helper atomically applies newcomer-pays capacity admission, fully allocates the requested bytes, expands ext4, and publishes an authority-bound receipt before L1 changes desired_disk_bytes. Job, attempt, Storage identity, and generation remain unchanged.

200.description: Identical grow replay.

202.description: Grow reserved; reconfiguration_phase remains growing until a helper receipt is accepted.

post.summary: Release a reconfiguration stranded on a dead bound Node
post.description: Typed escape hatch for a Computer stranded in backing_up, resetting, reimaging, growing, exporting, or importing. It requires exact CAS authority and a dead bound Node, preserves desired state, records uncertain artifacts for later removal, and requires explicit restart for recovery.

200.description: Identical abort replay.

202.description: Reconfiguration authority released; explicit restart or removal is now available.

post.summary: Reserve a new empty Storage generation
post.description: CAS operation that internally quiesces a running Computer only with explicit session termination and reserves generation+1 after capacity admission without fabricating operator stop intent. The bound agent fences the detached predecessor, fully allocates and verifies the tracked successor, and L1 durably publishes it; only then does shared removal delete and attest the predecessor before desired-running recovery resumes.

200.description: Identical reset replay; no second generation was reserved.

202.description: Reset reserved; reconfiguration_phase remains resetting until old-generation absence is verified.

get.summary: List current, staging, and retired Storage generations

200.description: Generation-ordered Storage lifecycle evidence.

get.summary: Project Storage provenance, managed custody forks, external taint, and exact removal outcomes
get.description: Returns durable L1 ledger facts only. A Custody import, or a Custody export that may have placed bytes outside managed custody, keeps custody_tainted true even after operator_attested_deleted; an export the helper refused before touching the destination (managed_root_path, external_path_unconfined, external_root_unmounted, or external_path_crosses_mount) does not taint; each managed branch independently reports removed_reduced versus removed_verified.

200.description: Storage provenance and custody graph facts.

get.summary: List immutable logical Backups and their managed source-node copy

parameters.name: backup_id
parameters.description: Also return that Backup operation's own observed state as `operation`, so a caller follows the operation it started rather than the latest one. 404 when the Computer has no such operation.

200.description: Backup records with Storage provenance and physical copy lifecycle.

post.summary: Create a fully allocated cold Backup under exact Computer and Storage authority
post.description: This one disruptive intent auto-quiesces a running Computer, plans the source-node copy before bytes are written, publishes only after full allocation and digest verification, and resumes only unchanged desired-running intent. Stopped stays stopped and stop or remove wins races.

allow_power_off.description: Required true when the Computer's authoritative desired state is running; acknowledges cold-copy quiescence and unchanged-intent resume.

200.description: Identical creation replay. The Backup headers name the operation this key started, not the Computer's latest one.

202.description: Backup intent planned; reconfiguration remains backing_up until the exact receipt is accepted.

post.summary: Explicitly prune one managed Backup copy
post.description: Capacity never auto-deletes a Backup. The immutable record becomes pruned only after an authority-bound positive absence receipt.

200.description: Identical prune replay.

post.summary: Restore a stopped Computer into exactly generation plus one
post.description: Requires stopped and positively detached authority, precommits the optional old-generation Backup identity, verifies a fully allocated copy before atomic publication, rotates stale authority, retires the predecessor, and never resumes the Computer.

200.description: Identical restore replay. Restore-Operation-Revision names the restore this key started, not the Computer's latest operation.

202.description: Restore reserved; the Computer remains stopped through verification, publication, and predecessor retirement.

parameters.name: computer_id
parameters.description: Source Computer that owns the Backup.

post.summary: Create a stopped Computer with fresh Computer and Storage identities and a fresh machine-id
post.description: Copies no grants, requires a new name, rejects a smaller destination, fully allocates and expands a larger destination, rekeys only the machine-id (SSH host keys and every other identity file are copied unchanged), preserves browser profile bytes, and records a Storage provenance custody fork.

200.description: Identical clone replay. Clone-Computer-Id and Clone-Operation-Revision name the clone this key started, not the destination's latest operation.

202.description: Clone reserved and not claimable until its source-copy receipt is accepted.

post.summary: Permanently record external custody before writing the first byte
post.description: The accepted event immediately reduces removal truth for this Storage provenance branch and descendants. Completion is separate assertion-derived evidence; interruption never retracts the event.

200.description: Identical Custody export replay.

202.description: Custody event committed before external bytes. From here the source Storage counts as custody-tainted, permanently, unless the helper refuses the export before touching the destination (managed_root_path, external_path_unconfined, external_root_unmounted, or external_path_crosses_mount).

get.summary: List permanent external custody events and non-upgrading deletion attestations

200.description: Custody events ordered by record time.

post.summary: Record operator_attested_deleted without upgrading removal truth

200.description: Attestation recorded or identically replayed; removed_reduced remains the strongest possible outcome.

post.summary: Validate a Custody manifest and digest into a new stopped no-grant Computer
post.description: The exported event is untouched. The operator supplies the portable custody.json and chooses the current destination Node; import does not depend on the exporting L1 database or its frozen root instance. The destination name and identities are atomically reserved in the shared Storage-copy ledger, then published only after manifest, source digest, destination digest, and clone-style OS identity rekey evidence bind them. The manifest's Job specification is held to the Computer creation rule after idempotency replay: one naming a run in run_id or handoff_owner_run_id is refused with 403 run_identity_not_entitled and nothing is reserved.

200.description: Identical Custody import replay.

202.description: Import validation and managed materialization reserved atomically as a stopped, non-claimable Computer until positive evidence is accepted.

get.summary: Observe one accepted Custody import by its immutable operation identity
get.description: Returns the durable import ledger outcome even if a failed import released its reserved Computer identity. Completion and helper preparation outcomes are revision-bound, so polling cannot lose an event recorded before observation begins.

200.description: Current durable import outcome.

post.summary: Install the next immutable Job projection
post.description: One CAS intent stages the new Job. A running Computer enters projecting and internally quiesces its current observation without fabricating operator stop intent; repeating the same request after positive reap atomically transfers authority and advances applied_revision. The staged spec is held to the Computer creation rule: one naming a run in run_id or handoff_owner_run_id is refused with 403 run_identity_not_entitled before any revision is reserved.

202.description: Projection intent accepted; phase and applied_revision show whether transfer is still waiting for quiescence.

post.summary: Irreversibly foreclose a Computer's Jobs and attempts
post.description: CAS-records removed intent, revokes live attempt authority, deletes the Computer's grants, and prevents every existing or future Job projection from being claimed. Removal is composite: L1 plans deletion of every retained Backup copy, and a bound current Job enters the durable service-removal directive protocol, whose authenticated agent cleanup also deletes the Computer's managed Storage (or reports a typed cleanup quarantine) before its Slot is released. When cleanup finishes, or at once when no Node is bound, L1 records removal_outcome: removed_verified, or removed_reduced while another clone branch or external Custody may still hold the Storage's bytes.

202.description: Removal intent accepted and all Job start authority revoked.

get.summary: List operator-visible nodes
get.description: Returns a page of registered nodes with effective liveness computed from one read-only snapshot and pinned clock, ordered by stable node ID. State filters apply effective liveness before paging. Reads never run cleanup or take the database write lock; background reconciliation records transitions and attempt expiry on its configured cadence (default one second). Cursors bind the exact filters and freeze insertion membership for a walk, excluding later inserts even when their IDs sort earlier. Mutable state, claims intent, capability observations and operator facts are live per-page snapshots. An empty next_cursor ends the walk.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation cursor from the same filter query. Limit may change between pages.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Exact effective node liveness at the snapshot clock, applied before pagination. Recorded state can lag until background reconciliation.

parameters.name: claims_enabled
parameters.description: Exact durable claims intent; accepts only true or false.

parameters.name: capability
parameters.description: Exact advertised capability key whose JSON value is true. Missing and false entries do not match.

200.description: Current fleet state.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor, or an empty string on the last page.

get.summary: Read one operator-visible node
get.description: Returns the same Node projection as the fleet listing from one read-only snapshot and pinned clock. state shows effective liveness immediately; reads never run cleanup or take the database write lock. active_attempts and last_condition remain recorded facts until background reconciliation (default one second). Conditions and their since timestamps are never fabricated. Actions requiring recorded state, such as Computer reconfiguration abort needing a recorded dead Node, remain unavailable until it is recorded.

200.description: Current Node facts.

post.summary: Stop new claims on a node
post.description: Disables claims as durable operator intent while allowing active attempt authority to finish. The mutation is revision-guarded and is valid for dead nodes. A stale revision is refused as stale_intent_revision with revision details as defined in the shared Error schema.

200.description: Claims are durably disabled; liveness state is unchanged.

post.summary: Set durable node claim intent
post.description: Stale intent revisions return stale_intent_revision with revision details as defined in the shared Error schema. Atomically enables or disables new claims when intent_revision matches. Liveness does not gate the write, and changing intent does not fence active attempts.

200.description: Updated node intent and projection.

post.summary: Reserved warm-session prompt
post.description: Reserved alongside awaiting-input; always returns 501 in v0.1.

post.summary: Cancel a queued or active one-shot
post.description: Atomically ends a queued one-shot as failed with job-level outcome canceled; no attempt or process result is invented. Requeued OCI jobs retain earlier attempt evidence. The originating client submitter, a current untagged person admin, or the live attempt credential of the immediate parent may cancel; authority is revalidated in the transaction. A bearer selects only parent scope and must arrive from the holding node. Out-of-scope and unknown targets return 404 not_found. Already-terminal one-shots and retries return the current job unchanged. Services return 409 cancel_service with desired_state_path and remove_path in error.details: the job routes with class=service, or for a Computer's job its /v1/computers/{computer_id} routes together with computer_id. For claimed, running and awaiting-input process or OCI one-shots, durably reserves outcome canceled and a fixed settlement deadline 30 seconds after acceptance. The state remains active pending settlement. Renewal and heartbeat deliver an attempt-fenced cancel directive for TERM, grace, then KILL. Completion after acceptance keeps its actual attempt result but settles the job failed/canceled, including a TERM-handler exit zero. Lease loss or deadline reconciliation settles a silent node without claiming runtime termination. Cancellation revokes new start acknowledgements and new child creation; identical child dispatch retries still return the stored job after credential revalidation; logs, late evidence and result uploads retain existing provenance rules. Cancellation also covers OCI image preparation, helper admission and durable Started; cancellation overrides pre-start runtime-unavailable requeue, including completion replay. OCI results are read before normal reap and uploaded and retained under existing rules. Removed services also receive the typed cancel_service refusal when cancellation authority is retained. Unsupported job classes or states return 409 cancel_not_queued. Cancellation refusals are non-retryable. Children are never canceled automatically. No request body or class selector is required; cancel determines the target class itself and ignores the read-route class selector.

200.description: Current job, including any cancellation outcome and retained attempt evidence.
